with the growth of conferences, one down side of expansion has jumped out with a vengeance...some schools rarely play each other.

this is especially true in the SEC and ACC with 14 teams and only 8 games.

so how you you solve this problem? I mean college football is based on its traditions, right? that is one major thing that gives the sport so much passion. so let's look at some of this history...

for different conferences, the concept of playing everyone had different degrees of importance. for instance. the old Big 8, played everyone going back generations. even in the days of fewer games. Take a look at Oklahoma's record 47 game win streak starting in 1953:

http://cfbdatawarehouse.com/data/active/o/oklahoma/1950-1954_yearly_results.php

their schedule was: The Big 8 + Texas + 1 or 2 other OOC games + bowl game. that is not that much variation in the schedule.

now look at Alabama during the same time:

They would play 6 or 7 teams in the 12 team SEC + several regional teams + bowl.

so traditionally, playing everyone in conference was far more important in the Big 8 than in the SEC. we see those traditions carried over into the modern Big 12 and the SEC.

there is nothing wrong with the Big 12 playing everybody every year (other than they are ignoring a great geographical fit in a recruiting hotbed state...). and there is nothing wrong with the SEC/ACC having huge gaps between cross division foes playing each other. as long as the main rivalries are preserved, either way works.

how important is it to preserve the rich history between Tennessee and LSU? http://cfbdatawarehouse.com/data/active/t/tennessee/opponents_records.php?teamid=1793 32 games while being in the same conference for 94 years

or Alabama - Kentucky
http://cfbdatawarehouse.com/data/active/a/alabama/opponents_records.php?teamid=1628 38 games while being in the same conference for 95 years

or UGA - Miss State http://cfbdatawarehouse.com/data/active/g/georgia/opponents_records.php?teamid=2049

23 games while being in the same conference for 95 years

so the answer to the question of "how often do teams need to play each other in conference is: it depends on the conference.

that's my take on it anyway.
